description: Erection of a second floor and mansard roof extension together with ground and first floor rear extension together with associated alterations including roof terrace to provide a 6 bedroom 7 occupant HMO (Sui Generis).
decision_conditions:
The Development hereby permitted shall only be carried out and completed strictly in accordance with the submitted plans hereby approved and any subsequent approval of details.


REASON: To ensure that the development hereby permitted is carried out in full accordance with the plans hereby approved.

<p>Sound Insulation between Residential and Commercial Properties </p><p>Sound insulation shall be installed between the commercial premises on the first floor and residential premises on the second floor. The applicant shall provide a scheme of sound insulation that shall be submitted for approval to the Council’s Noise Section before the commencement of works.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To obtain required sound insulation and prevent noise nuisance.</p>

The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission.


REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

<p>A post installation test shall be carried out prior to occupation to demonstrate that all residential premises designed in accordance with “BS8233:2014 - Guidance on Sound Insulation and Noise Reduction for Buildings” achieve the required internal noise levels cited in Table of Condition 1 above have been met and the results submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To obtain required sound insulation and prevent noise nuisance.</p>

<p>The use hereby permitted, or the operation of any building services plant, shall not commence until a post-installation noise assessment has been carried out to confirm compliance with the noise criteria. The scheme shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and attenuation measures, and they shall be permanently retained and maintained in working order for the duration of the use and their operation.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To protect the amenities of adjoining occupiers and the surrounding area.</p>

<p>All residential premises shall be designed in accordance with BS8233:2014 'Guidance on sound insulation and noise reduction for buildings' to attain the following noise levels:</p><ul><li>Living rooms (Resting): 35dB LAeq,16hrs (7am to 11pm)&nbsp; </li><li>Dining room/area (Dining): 40dB LAeq,16hrs (7am to 11pm)&nbsp; </li><li>Bedrooms (Sleeping): 35dB LAeq,16hrs (7am to 11pm) and 30dB LAeq,8hrs (11pm to 7am)&nbsp; </li></ul><p><br></p><p>REASON: To obtain required sound insulation and prevent noise nuisance.</p>

<p>Prior to the commencement of relevant above ground works, full details and physical samples of all facing materials to be used on the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted including facing brickwork (matching London stock brick sample panel), window frames (timber sash), and roof coverings (natural slate) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. </p><p>The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details as approved and shall be permanently maintained as such thereafter.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To ensure that the external appearance of the building is satisfactory and does not prejudice the visual amenity of the area.</p>

<p>Prior to the occupation of the development hereby approved, details and full specifications of 1 bird boxes, and 1 swift bricks/boxes shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority and shall be maintained for the lifespan of the development. The details should include:</p><ul><li>A minimum of 1 swift bricks (same requirements for swift box) incorporated into the design of the development. They should be installed in groups of at least 2, and placed at or close to eaves level of the development hereby approved. They should be placed at least 5m above the ground with a 5m unobstructed flight path, both below and in front of the swift brick. The swift brick should be located facing north, east, or north east (direct sunlight should be avoided) and should not be placed immediately above doors or windows. Where possible, swift bricks should be set flush into the external wall to match adjacent brickwork.</li><li>A minimum of 1 bird boxes incorporated into the design of the development, with a variety of box types (including different sized entrance holes) to provide habitat for diverse bird species. The boxes should be installed at or close to the eaves level of the development hereby approved. The boxes should be between 3 and 5 metres from the ground, and there should be a clear flight path without any obstructions below and directly in front of the box. The boxes should be facing north, east or north east (direct sunlight should be avoided), and should not be placed immediately above doors or windows. Boxes located in the same area should not be placed too close together.&nbsp;</li></ul><p><br></p><p>REASON: To support bird populations, including swifts, in Hackney and preserve endangered urban biodiversity, by providing nesting opportunities, in accordance with Hackney’s Local Plan LP33 policy LP47.</p>

<p>No development shall commence until a Construction Logistics Plan (CLP) and Construction Management Plan (CMP) have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include:</p><p>a) Construction phase environmental management overview, including site description and management responsibilities;</p><p>b) Site working hours (08:00 to 18:00 Monday to Friday; 08:00 to 13:00 Saturdays; and at no time on Sundays or Bank Holidays);</p><p>c) Detailed site logistics and delivery arrangements for Stoke Newington Road, including clear loading/unloading zones, delivery times, and measures to prevent construction vehicles queuing or blocking the public highway;&nbsp; </p><p>d) On-site storage locations for plant, scaffolding, refuse, and construction materials to ensure no encroachment onto the public footway;</p><p>e) Measures to control dust, noise, and vibration during demolition and construction works, including the identification of sensitive neighbouring receptors and deployment of mitigation measures;&nbsp; </p><p>f) Measures to prevent the deposit of mud and debris on the public highway; and</p><p>g) Contact details of a named site manager responsible for community liaison, handling resident inquiries, and resolving highway concerns.</p><p>The development shall thereafter be implemented strictly in accordance with the approved details throughout the construction period, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To ensure that the development does not prejudice highway safety, cause undue obstruction on the public highway, or result in unacceptable harm to the amenity of neighbouring occupiers.</p>

<p>Prior to superstructure works, detailed specification, a drainage layout and a management &amp;
maintenance plan (where applicable) of at least one suitable sustainable drainage system (i.e.
water butt with overflow, raingarden, bioretention planter box, living roof (substrate depth of 80-
150mm excluding the vegetative mat), permeable paving etc.) shall be submitted to, and
approved by the LPA, in consultation with the LLFA. If soakaways i.e. plastic modules and
soakaway rings are used, an infiltration test must be carried out to ensure that the capacity of the
soil is suitable for infiltration. It must be demonstrated that there will be no increase in surface
water flow being discharged offsite and an overall reduction in peak flow rate and volume.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: In the interest of sustainable urban drainage.</p>

<p>Commercial Kitchen Extract System</p><p>Any new plant shall be installed, together with any associated ancillary equipment, so as to prevent the transmission of noise and vibration into neighbouring premises. The rated noise level from all plant and ancillary equipment shall not increase the existing background noise level (10dB below) when measured 1m external from the nearest residential or noise sensitive premises. An assessment of the expected noise levels shall be carried out by a suitably qualified (IOA accredited) and experienced acoustic consultant, in accordance with BS 4142:2014+A1:2019 ‘Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound,’ and any mitigation measures necessary to achieve the above required noise levels shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in writing for approval.</p><p>The plant shall thereafter be installed and maintained in accordance with the approved details.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To protect acceptable local noise levels.</p>

<p>Prior to the first occupation of the residential unit hereby approved, details of a privacy screen (including height, design, and materials) to be installed on the southern perimeter of the second-floor roof terrace shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved privacy screen shall be installed in full prior to the first occupation of the terrace and shall be permanently retained as such thereafter.&nbsp; </p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To safeguard the privacy and residential amenity of neighbouring occupiers.</p>
